Choose the authorised recipient and the exact decision you need before adapting the message. Keep only the options and dates that apply; the example is not a required timetable.

Use this to request a decision, protection or intervention when the ordinary route has not resolved the issue or is inappropriate. Use emergency or specialist reporting routes directly when urgent.

## Privacy screen

- [ ] I am contacting the correct authorised recipient.
- [ ] I have included only information needed for this decision.
- [ ] Sensitive evidence is stored in an approved location, not broadly attached.
- [ ] I have avoided speculation about motives or diagnoses.
- [ ] I have named any immediate safety, participant, privacy or integrity concern clearly.

## Completed example

*Illustrative example; replace these details with your own verified record.*

**Subject:** Supervision review decision needed by 22 September: ethics submission dependency

Hello Graduate Research Coordinator,

I am requesting help to secure or reassign the review needed before my ethics submission can proceed.

My recruitment flow and three review questions were sent to my principal supervisor on 2 September under our agreed two-week review window. I followed up on 17 September and have not received a response. The ethics package requires five working days after this decision and is due on 30 September.

I have completed the other package checks and asked my co-supervisor whether they can review it. The dated requests and current package are in the approved supervision record.

The feasible options are: agree a review time this week; authorise the co-supervisor to complete this review; or revise the milestone through the formal process. I recommend confirming the co-supervisor review by 22 September while retaining principal-supervisor visibility.

Could you advise or decide the appropriate route by 22 September? No participant-facing work will begin before written approval.

Regards,

[name]

## Check your record

Check that the recipient can take the requested action. Retain the reply and next decision in the appropriate record; sending the message does not resolve the issue.

## Scenario test

If the supervisor is implicated in bullying or retaliation, do not send this message to them as the only route. Use an independent complaints, safety, advocacy or graduate research contact. Keep sensitive evidence out of an ordinary shared supervision folder.

## Evidence of done

Record the response, decision, owner, due date and resulting changes. “Message sent” does not prove the issue was resolved.
